Cyber Attack Disrupts Cyprus Construction Materials Firms

A major cyber attack has disrupted operations at several construction materials companies in Cyprus, including Vassiliko Cement Works Ltd, causing widespread delays in supply and uncertainty in the sector. The incident, believed to be a sophisticated ransomware assault, began late Tuesday night and is ongoing as of Wednesday afternoon.

According to industry sources, the attack has crippled key IT systems, affecting logistics, order processing, and invoicing platforms. Vassiliko Cement Works Ltd confirmed that “certain digital services are temporarily unavailable as we work with cybersecurity experts to resolve the situation.” The company emphasized that production lines remain operational, but deliveries and customer communications are facing delays.

Another affected company, Nicosia Aggregates Ltd, reported that their administrative and dispatch systems have also been compromised. Local construction projects are already feeling the impact, with site managers reporting difficulties in receiving scheduled shipments of cement, aggregates, and ready-mix concrete.

“We have trucks waiting at plants, but the systems needed to approve and release orders are down,” said Christos Kyriakides, spokesperson for the Cyprus Construction Materials Association. “This is a critical period for the industry, with several major infrastructure projects underway.”

The full extent of the attack is still unclear, and experts warn that recovery could take several days. The Ministry of Energy, Commerce and Industry has been notified and is monitoring the situation closely.

“We urge all companies in the sector to increase vigilance and follow best cybersecurity practices,” said a ministry official. “Our priority is to restore operations and minimize disruption.”

Analysts predict that if the outage persists, construction timelines across the island could face significant setbacks.
